scenes.title: The plan
scenes.vo: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: First, Transaction simulation: good wallets (and tools like transaction simulators) show the expected balance changes before you sign: "minus 100 U.S.D.C., +0.033 ETH". If the preview shows assets leaving that you didn't intend, stop. Next, Typed-data signatures (EIP-712): structured messages (orders, Permits) that your wallet shows as fields. Read the spender, token, amount and deadline. A "Permit" or "Permit2" signature can hand over token access without any gas. Then, Blind signing: when a hardware wallet can't decode a transaction, it shows only a hash. Keep blind signing off by default; turn it on only for a specific, verified action, then off again. Also, Account delegation (EIP-7702): since Ethereum's 2025 Pectra upgrade, a normal wallet can sign an authorisation that delegates its behaviour to a smart contract. A malicious delegation can hand control of the whole account to an attacker. Only sign delegations from wallets and apps you trust, for a stated purpose. And finally, Rule: if you can't say in one sentence what a prompt does, don't sign it.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: A site asks you to "verify your wallet".
The wallet shows a typed-data message
Reject it, close the tab, and check your approvals.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. A site asks you to "verify your wallet". The wallet shows a typed-data message: Permit2 times token: U.S.D.C. , spender: 0x9f…c3 times amount: 115792089… (unlimited) , deadline: 2030. That isn't verification: it's unlimited U.S.D.C. access for an unknown spender. Reject it, close the tab, and check your approvals.
scenes.cap: Let's work an example, step by step. A site asks you to "verify your wallet". The wallet shows a typed-data message: Permit2 · token: USDC · spender: 0x9f…c3 · amount: 115792089… (unlimited) · deadline: 2030. That isn't verification: it's unlimited USDC access for an unknown spender. Reject it, close the tab, and check your approvals.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: My wallet shows simulated balance changes before signing
I read spender, token, amount and deadline on every typed-data prompt
Blind signing is off on my hardware wallet
I never sign account-delegation requests from unknown sites

scenes.q: Why is a Permit signature risky if you don't read it?
scenes.a: It can grant token access without a transaction or gas, so it's easy to approve by accident.
